tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when a training job is denied access...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (fails, hangs, denied access, capacity errors) rather than internal implementation, explicitly covers many trigger contexts even when the user does not name the domain directly ('even if they do not mention execution roles, key policies...'), and remains a concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a training job is denied access to S3, a KMS key or iam:PassRole, fails with InsufficientInstanceCapacity, ResourceLimitExceeded or out of memory... even if they do not mention execution roles, key policies, checkpoint paths, metric definitions, security groups or data channels by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into domain-specific procedures, check-ids, and router tables rather than explaining general concepts like what SageMaker or training jobs are. It stays tightly focused on this skill's specific diagnostic workflow.
tests.evidence: Grounded in the LLM-SM check family under checks-sagemaker-training.md — the LLM-SM-TRAIN-* sub-family for training / customization; load it before assigning any check-id or severity.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body contains only an index table (what-it-catches) and router pointers, with full detection rules, remediations, and citations explicitly deferred to references/checks-sagemaker-training.md rather than embedded inline.
tests.evidence: The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference — the table below is a what-it-catches index.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five reference files are linked via markdown links in the body: checks-sagemaker-training.md, collection-reference.md, api-quirks.md, known-causes.md, and metrics-and-logs.md all appear with markdown link syntax.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with a clear trigger condition for when to load it, e.g. tied to specific symptoms or check-ids in the router table and elsewhere.
tests.evidence: Load known-causes.md whenever the user names an error or symptom; match it to a section, check the cited AWS page, and give the cause, how to confirm it, and the fix.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (classification, severity assignment, read-only guardrails) are given exact prescriptive steps and checklists, while explanatory 'why' content (e.g., capacity vs quota distinction) is included to help the agent generalize; flexible areas like how to phrase remediation are left open.
tests.evidence: The capacity-vs-quota split is opposite remediations — read both the FailureReason and the quota value (api-quirks.md §2).

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill does not present multiple competing tools/approaches as equal menu options; it specifies exact APIs to call per scenario via the router table, without offering alternatives without defaults.
tests.evidence: My training job failed, the data looks corrupt or won't parse | DescribeTrainingJob FailureReason, then the JSONL sample

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure and Router teach a generalizable diagnostic approach (classify status, bucket failure cause, confirm artifacts) applicable to any training job, not a one-off declaration for a specific job instance.
tests.evidence: Step 3: If Failed, bucket the FailureReason into exactly one cause and cite the check: malformed data (LLM-SM-TRAIN-001) / AWS-side capacity (LLM-SM-TRAIN-002) ...

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' section plus an 'Error Handling' section documenting non-obvious API quirks and traps specific to this domain.
tests.evidence: 'The job is InProgress with Pending, so it is failing.' A job waiting on GPU capacity is control-plane-healthy, not Failed.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces health reports and findings, and it provides an explicit output template asset for full reports.
tests.evidence: Use training-job-health-report-template.md when a full report is requested.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output template exists in the body; the health report template is stored in assets/ and referenced rather than embedded.
tests.evidence: Use [training-job-health-report-template.md](assets/training-job-health-report-template.md) when a full report is requested.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is referenced in the body via markdown link.
tests.evidence: [training-job-health-report-template.md](assets/training-job-health-report-template.md) — load when a full report is requested

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset reference specifies the condition for loading it (when a full report is requested).
tests.evidence: load when a full report is requested: training/customization report format (per-job state, failure classification, findings, cost note, disclosed scope).

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure, which is the main ordered, dependent workflow, is formatted as a checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' labeling as required.
tests.evidence:
- [ ] Step 1: ListTrainingJobs / DescribeTrainingJob ... 
- [ ] Step 2: Classify Pending-vs-Failed. ...

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit 'Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' section instructing the agent to check its own findings against specific criteria before presenting.
tests.evidence: A wrong or unsupported finding is worse than a slow one. Before presenting, re-check your output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion.
